history.dynasty: Awadh Nawabi period (Raja Tikait Rai, Diwan of the Nawab of Awadh)
history.period: ~17th century (local tradition says the temple is about 400 years old)
history.summary: The Sheetla Devi temple at Tikaitganj, Lucknow, dedicated to Goddess Sheetala, a form of Shakti worshipped as the curer of diseases (especially smallpox). Local accounts say the temple was ruined by invaders and revived when a local businessman found the Devi idol in a nearby water tank. Raja Tikait Rai, then Diwan of the Nawab, is credited with foreseeing the temple's construction and building a pond nearby that is still called 'Tikait Rai ka Talab'. Sheetal Ashtami is the main festival, on which the goddess is traditionally offered stale prasad. Note: no verified photograph of this specific Tikaitganj temple could be found, so media is empty.

name: Shri Sheetala Devi Temple
town_description: Lucknow is the capital of Uttar Pradesh, on the banks of the Gomti river. It was the seat of the Nawabs of Awadh and is famed for its Awadhi culture, cuisine, tehzeeb, and Indo-Islamic architecture such as the Bara Imambara and Rumi Darwaza.

travel.airport: Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport, Lucknow (~10 km)
travel.road: Tikaitganj, Rajajipuram area of Lucknow; connected by city buses, auto-rickshaws and taxis
